title: Command Injection via scala.sys.process Interpolator
platform_conditions: Scala 2.13 / Scala 3 standard library (scala.sys.process, scala.tools reflection) on the JVM
security_mechanism: scala.sys.process converts a plain String into a shell command line: the string form ("cmd".!) hands the text to the platform shell, so an interpolated value containing ';' or '|' becomes a second command. Building the string with an interpolator (s"sh -c $x") is exactly the dangerous form, while Seq("cmd", arg) constructs an argv vector with no shell involved. On the code-execution side, the reflection ToolBox (scala.tools.reflect.ToolBox) compiles and evaluates a source string, and a script-engine eval in Scala/JVM syntax executes it identically.

source_sink_clues.source: Request parameters, filenames, or configuration values interpolated into process command strings or reflection-evaluated source text.
source_sink_clues.sink: String-typed scala.sys.process builders ("...".! / .!! / Process("...")) with interpolation; ToolBox.eval; ScriptEngine.eval on attacker text

tracking_guards: Check the process is built from Seq(executable, args...) with a fixed executable path and the dynamic value as one element; check '--' or equivalent option-terminators precede attacker arguments; check no ToolBox/eval path is reachable from input.
not_candidate_when: The command is a constant with no interpolation, the dynamic value is validated against a strict grammar (numeric/identifier) before use, or the call takes the Seq argv form.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html
Scala standard library: scala.sys.process (no stable deep-link cited)
